solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: See 20
Is crossword an ancient game or a foreign friend?

parts.note: the puzzle speaking of itself asks this question in the first person, so the words become am I
Go is an ancient East Asian board game of stones on a grid

explanation.surface: A whimsical question: is this puzzle an old pastime or a pal from abroad?
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is the crossword speaking about itself: 'Is crossword ...?' put in its own voice becomes 'Am I ...?'; 'an' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is the Spanish word for a pal, borrowed into English for a friend from another country.

clue.text: In top half of missile, burn oxygen fuel

indicators.note: in places the burning and oxygen pieces inside the shortened weapon
the top half of a down entry is its first half, so only the first three letters of the projectile are kept

parts.note: a bullet is a small missile fired from a gun
to burn in the sun is to tan
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Instructions for a rocket: inside the upper half of the projectile, combust oxygen as propellant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top half of' takes the first half because this is a down entry, where the top of a word comes first; 'In' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Butanol is an alcohol that can be burned as a motor fuel or blended with petrol.

clue.text: Reveals misjudgments in trumps

parts.note: to out someone is to reveal a secret about them, so reveals gives outs
trips are slips or mistakes, so misjudgments gives trips

explanation.surface: A card player exposes errors in the choice of trumps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trumps' looks like the card-game noun but is the verb meaning beats or outdoes.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstrip someone is to surpass them, and to trump someone is likewise to outdo them.

clue.text: Money one lost to small, mischievous being — the compiler

indicators.note: lost tells us the letters of one go missing from the word money

parts.note: taken as written, the word one spelt out
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
an elf is a small mischievous sprite in folklore

explanation.surface: Someone loses cash to a tiny prankish sprite, says the puzzle's setter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' takes O, N and E out of MONEY in order, leaving MY. Setters often refer to themselves as 'the compiler', meaning the person writing.
explanation.definitionFit: When a crossword setter writes about the compiler, the setter means their own self, the first person.

clue.text: Loftily call for peasant after heart transplant

indicators.note: a heart transplant swaps the central organ, so the central letter of the rustic is replaced by another

parts.note: a yokel is an unsophisticated country person or peasant

explanation.surface: A country bumpkin shouts from on high after cardiac surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of YOKEL is K; 'heart transplant' swaps it for D. The clue does not say which letter goes in, so the definition decides it.
explanation.definitionFit: A yodel is a warbling cry sung high in the Alps, so it is a call made loftily.

clue.text: Feature to view on top of hill

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: to eye something is to view it
the brow of a hill is its top

explanation.surface: A scenic feature: a place to take in the view at the summit of a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top of hill' is not a first-letter pick: the whole phrase defines the summit word. 'on' is the down-entry convention, putting the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyebrow is one of the features of the face, the arch of hair above each eye.

clue.text: Story about account I put together for mathematician

parts.note: a fib is a small lie or tall story
on means about or concerning, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A fake tale about bookkeeping, assembled for a numbers expert.
explanation.definitionFit: Fibonacci was a medieval Italian mathematician, known for the number sequence named after him.

clue.text: Law court at end outwardly

indicators.note: outwardly says the word for end goes round the outside of the other pieces

parts.note: to die is to end or come to a stop
taken as written

explanation.surface: A legal case reaches the bench at the close, viewed from outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end' is a verb here, a synonym for perish, not a position indicator; 'outwardly' makes it the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictate is a command or rule laid down with authority, which is what a law is.

clue.text: Bowling initially for a short time, puffs hard and quickly, perhaps

indicators.note: for signals that one letter is put in place of another in the word for puffs

parts.note: a puff is a promotional advertisement, so puffs are adverts
T is the usual abbreviation of time, a word shortened to one letter

indicators.note: initially says to take only the opening letter of bowling

explanation.surface: A cricketer's opening ball, in brief, comes after huffing, fast and furiously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps the T (time, shortened) in ADVERTS for B, the first letter of 'Bowling'. 'hard and quickly' are not about effort: they are examples of a part of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard and quickly are both words that modify verbs, so they are examples of that grammatical class.

clue.text: In lab, heater brewed liquid concoction

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients up, so the letters of the two words are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A drink is made in a laboratory using a heating appliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewed' rearranges LAB and HEATER.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbal infusion is a drink made by steeping plants in hot water, a liquid concoction.

clue.text: Won the deal — might be broke?

indicators.note: might be hints that the words could become something else when their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Winning a hand at cards, or a business deal, yet you could still be penniless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might be' rearranges WON THE DEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Being down-at-heel means shabby and poor, like someone whose shoe heels have worn down, so short of money.

clue.text: Phoned and spoke

definitions.meaning: having telephoned someone, past participle of the verb for calling
a crosspiece of a ladder or chair, the noun sense, not the past tense of speak

explanation.surface: Someone made a call and had a chat.
explanation.definitionFit: Rung is the past participle of ring, to telephone, and also a ladder's crossbar, like a spoke.

clue.text: Hot ingredient for foodstore in Indian city

indicators.note: an ingredient goes inside a dish, so the letter for hot is placed within the shop

parts.note: a deli, short for delicatessen, is a shop selling prepared foods
H is the usual abbreviation of hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A spicy element suits a food shop in a city of India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ingredient for' puts H inside DELI.
explanation.definitionFit: Delhi is a major city in northern India, home of the capital New Delhi.

clue.text: Loud hiding place is beside a fen in grassland

indicators.note: a hiding place conceals something, here the answer within the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A noisy spot to lurk sits next to a marsh in pasture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding place' looks like DEN, but it is the signal: the answer runs through besiDE A FEN IN Grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: Deafening describes a sound so loud it could take away one's hearing.

clue.text: See 20
Thing for sitting on board starts first

indicators.note: first says those opening letters come at the front, before the word for sitting
starts tells us to take only the opening letters of on and board

parts.note: a sitting of a committee or court is a session

explanation.surface: A seat to sit in, for when you board, with first dibs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' takes O and B from 'on board'; 'first' puts them in front of SESSION.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a thing for something is an idiom for being fixated on it, so a thing is a fixation.

clue.text: Party line goes round in circles, to people's amusement

definitions.text: goes round in circles, to people's amusement

parts.note: to carouse is to party with drinking and noise, and a carouse is such a party

explanation.surface: A political party's policy keeps circling, entertaining onlookers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party line' looks like a political phrase but splits into CAROUSE and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A carousel is a fairground roundabout that turns in circles to amuse riders.

clue.text: I'm up to top of my potential?

definitions.text: I'm up to top of my potential?

indicators.note: potential suggests the letters could form something else, so the preceding words are rearranged
in a down entry the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of reaching the peak of their abilities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potential' rearranges I'M UP TO; 'top of' adds M from 'my'. The whole clue also describes the best one can reach.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up to the limit of one's potential is reaching the best achievable level, the ideal.

clue.text: Openings of songs can influence fans in this genre

indicators.note: openings are beginnings, so only the first letter of each following word is used

explanation.surface: The way music begins can sway listeners of a particular style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Openings of' takes the first letters of 'songs can influence fans in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Science fiction is a literary and film category, the genre the clue points to.

clue.text: President to forbid a Japanese arrangement

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of US President Dwight Eisenhower
to ban is to forbid

explanation.surface: A US leader bans a deal made in Tokyo.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikebana is the Japanese art of flower arranging.

clue.text: Team playing scrabble win with "moo"

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of the following words are being juggled about, like tiles in a board game

explanation.surface: A side playing a board game of words scores a win with the word for a cow's call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges SCRABBLE, WIN, WITH and MOO, eighteen letters in all, into the three-word club name; the board game looks like the team's activity but is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: West Bromwich Albion is an English professional football club, so it is an example of a team.

clue.text: Groom has wit and style

parts.note: to groom someone is to dress or tidy them up
wit means good sense, as in having the wits to act

explanation.surface: A bridegroom is both clever and fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' looks like the man at a wedding but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Dress sense is a flair for choosing clothes well, a kind of personal style.

clue.text: Energy tax demand for chauffeur

definitions.meaning: vigour or push, as in a person with plenty of get-up-and-go
to strain or overwork, as when people are pushed hard
the order given to a hired ... to set off

explanation.surface: Vigour is needed by the taxman demanding payment for a hired driver.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: 'tax demand' looks like one phrase but splits between the second and third senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive means vigour, means to push someone hard, and is the instruction given to a chauffeur.

clue.text: From coasts, see child aboard ship

indicators.note: aboard puts the young person inside the ship abbreviation

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A voyager watches the shoreline while a youngster travels on a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coasts' looks like shorelines but is the verb: to glide along without effort.
explanation.definitionFit: To skid is to slide along without grip, much as a vehicle that coasts glides on without power.

clue.text: Lay armour by post far away

parts.note: a lay is a song or ballad, and so is an air
mail is armour made of linked metal rings

explanation.surface: Send a knight's armour off to a distant land through the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay' looks like a verb but is the old word for a song.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmail is post carried by aircraft, typically for sending letters abroad over long distances.

clue.text: It is healthy to consume contents of Ovid before the majority of training

indicators.note: before places the Latin poet's inner letters ahead of the shortened training word
the contents of a word are its inner letters, without the first and last
the majority of a word is most of it, here all but its final letter

parts.note: taming is the training of a wild animal

explanation.surface: A health tip: absorb the poet Ovid and most of your workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'training' is taming, as of a wild animal, not exercise; 'the majority of' drops its last letter and 'contents of' strips the poet's name to its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A vitamin is a nutrient the body needs in small amounts, something good for you to take.

clue.text: One pierces and flips fighter plane before barrier

indicators.note: before places the turned jet ahead of the barrier word
flips means the jet's name is turned round and read the other way

parts.note: a MiG is a Soviet or Russian fighter jet
a let is an obstruction or hindrance, as in without let or hindrance

explanation.surface: An airman in a fighter does acrobatics before hitting a barricade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flips' turns MIG into GIM.
explanation.definitionFit: A gimlet is a small hand tool for boring holes, so it is something that pierces.

clue.text: Loudly demands massages

indicators.note: loudly means spoken out loud, so the word for demands is heard rather than read

parts.note: to need is to require or demand

explanation.surface: Someone insists noisily on a rubdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loudly' signals a sound-alike: NEEDS said out loud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To knead is to work and press muscles with the hands, which is how massages are given.
